text: Where would a CIO get surprised by hidden data readiness gaps in back-office AI?
claudePromptBoundary: Full production prompt is reconstructed from current source template and captured source packet. ai_egress_audit stores prompt hash/snapshot refs, not raw prompt text by default.
claudeResponse:
Lakeshore Holdings has four specific places where a CIO gets ambushed by data readiness gaps — and your loaded evidence already signals three of them clearly. The first surprise is spreadsheet-sovereign data masquerading as a system.
Your IT landscape shows a "Treasury spreadsheet control repository" feeding 91,000 daily transactions directly into Claude Code via a bank connectivity interface. That is not a controlled data source — it is a manual artifact being treated as one. Any AI model consuming it inherits undocumented assumptions, version risk, and audit exposure.
The gap is invisible until a payment anomaly or SOX test surfaces it. The second is semantic ownership nobody has claimed. You have a dbt semantic layer feeding regional workflow apps at 94,600 daily volume, but the loaded sources show no named semantic owner for GL or management reporting definitions.
An AI that answers finance questions against an uncertified semantic layer will produce confident, wrong answers. That is a CIO-credibility event, not just a data quality issue. The third is source breadth without certification.
The KPI shows 68 data sources in scope at medium confidence — and explicitly flags that privilege constraints and readiness signals should be shown before any automation is recommended. Sixty-eight sources is enough surface area that a few unvetted ones will corrupt outputs for the ones that are clean.
